clue.text: Gold medal placing either way

indicators.note: either way says the answer reads identically from the left and from the right

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A remark about a winner's position on the podium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'either way' is the only wordplay: the two-word answer spells the same backwards as forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: First place, the gold medallist's position, is the highest spot on the podium.

clue.text: Cheap wood covered by tax

indicators.note: covered by means the wood sits inside the word for tax

parts.note: to try is to tax or strain, as in 'try one's patience'
ash is a tree and its timber

explanation.surface: Inexpensive timber burdened with a levy.
explanation.definitionFit: Trashy goods are low-grade and tawdry, so the word describes something cheap and nasty.

clue.text: Land in North America confiscated by parents

indicators.note: confiscated by means the continent abbreviation is held inside the word for parents

parts.note: pa and ma are both parents

explanation.surface: Property in North America seized by Mum and Dad.
explanation.walkthrough: PA and MA together hold NA.
explanation.definitionFit: Panama is a country, and a land is a nation or country.

clue.text: Prisoner flipping secure, flushed toilet

parts.note: POW is a prisoner of war

indicators.note: flipping in a down clue turns over the words for secure and flushed together

parts.note: to moor a boat is to secure it
flushed means red in the face

explanation.surface: An inmate turns over a lock, and the loo is flushed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' reverses MOOR and RED together, making DERROOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A powder room is a polite euphemism for a women's lavatory, so it means toilet.

clue.text: A kick, toe reaching head, off limits

indicators.note: the toe, the last letter, of the phrase travels up to its start

parts.note: to boot is to kick

explanation.surface: A footballer's kick sends the toe to the head, which is forbidden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toe reaching head' moves the T at the end of ABOOT to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taboo is forbidden by custom, so it is out of bounds.

clue.text: P for pillock?

parts.note: the letter P is the head of a pin and also the first letter of pillock

explanation.surface: A spelling-alphabet entry: P stands for pillock.
explanation.walkthrough: P is literally a pin's head as a letter: the head of the word 'pin'; and the whole word means a fool, which is what a pillock (British slang for an idiot) is.
explanation.definitionFit: A dimwit or fool is insultingly called this, as having a brain the size of a pin's tip.

clue.text: See 12
Items securing screws — having one loose?

definitions.meaning: small threaded metal fittings that hold bolts or screws in place
having a screw loose means being crazy or mad

explanation.definitionFit: Hex fasteners hold screws in place, and the plural is slang for mad, like having a screw loose.

clue.text: Single part of wheel, big, I levered up

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the hidden letters read upwards, from bottom to top
part of means the answer lies within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Lone section of a wheel, large, which I prised up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of' takes ELBIGILE from wheEL BIG I LEvered, and 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: An eligible bachelor is an unmarried man, so eligible can mean single and available.

clue.text: Times, admitting sin under setter, confused person

indicators.note: under in a down clue places the multiplication word below the breed

parts.note: a setter is a breed of dog

indicators.note: admitting means the word for sin is let inside

parts.note: by means times in multiplication, as in 'three by four'
to err is to sin

explanation.surface: A newspaper, accepting a wrong from its puzzle compiler, is muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' looks like the puzzle's compiler but is the dog. Dogberry is the bumbling constable in Shakespeare's Much Ado About Nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's constable is famous for muddled speech and malapropisms, so he is a byword for a confused person.

clue.text: See 23
Stiff won't be pliable ultimately, in obsession with women's underwear?

indicators.note: in places the final letter of pliable within the word for the undergarment

parts.note: a bra is a piece of women's underwear

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the word pliable

parts.note: a thing is a fixation or obsession, as in 'have a thing about'

explanation.surface: A rigid man is unbending, perhaps thanks to a fetish for lingerie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stiff' is slang for a corpse, and a corpse won't be doing this. 'ultimately' takes E, the last letter of pliable, which 'in' places inside the undergarment.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead body has stopped drawing air into its lungs, so a corpse will not be respiring.

clue.text: Kinky Romeo in sexy diamonds, not entirely appreciated by gay people

indicators.note: in tells us the rearranged lover sits within the word for sexy

parts.note: hot is slang for sexy

indicators.note: kinky means twisted, so the letters of Romeo are rearranged
not entirely means the last letter of the slang word is dropped

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A lurid tale of a pervy lover dripping in jewels, enjoyed by a gay audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kinky' rearranges the lover's name to MOERO, which 'in' places within the word for sexy; 'not entirely' trims the slang for diamonds to IC.
explanation.definitionFit: Something erotic in a same-sex way appeals to gay people, being about sexual desire between men or women.

clue.text: Directive pens letters required for 16's second post

indicators.note: the letters of the preceding words are required in a new order, an instruction to rearrange them

explanation.surface: An order encloses lettering needed for a deputy job.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 is UNCLE SAM, so '16's second post' is America's second-highest office. 'letters required' tells you the letters of DIRECTIVE PENS are wanted rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The deputy to the US head of state holds the second-highest office in America.

clue.text: Insurrectionary services up for striking, possibly

indicators.note: insurrectionary means rebellious, overturning order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Rebellious religious services start, ready to strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Percussive describes instruments that are struck to make sound, like drums.

clue.text: See 20
Sweet girl

definitions.meaning: a dessert of fruit and sponge or bread in a mould

explanation.definitionFit: A charlotte is a moulded pudding, and it is also a woman's given name.

clue.text: America's endless nuclear missiles emptied and dismantled

indicators.note: dismantled means taken to pieces and put together again in a new order
endless means the word nuclear loses its final letter
emptied means only the outer letters of missiles remain

explanation.surface: The USA's nuclear rockets are being disarmed and broken up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' gives NUCLEA, 'emptied' gives MS, and 'dismantled' rearranges the lot; 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The bearded figure in a top hat is the personification of the United States.

clue.text: I bleed after a cold, water polluted

indicators.note: after puts the second pair of words behind the first pair

parts.note: to bleed a tank or radiator is to drain it

explanation.surface: Someone drains a radiator after catching a chill, and the water is dirty.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid rain is rainfall made harmful by pollutants in the air.

clue.text: Centre of Birmingham candlelit, perhaps: magical!

parts.note: the NEC, the National Exhibition Centre, is a big venue near Birmingham
a candlelit dinner is an example of something romantic

explanation.surface: Downtown Birmingham by candlelight is enchanting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Centre of Birmingham' looks like the middle letters of the city's name, but it is the NEC, the National Exhibition Centre, a large venue near Birmingham, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Necromancy is sorcery, especially raising the dead, so this adjective describes magic or wizardry.

clue.text: Country not quite accepting change, government department restraining new 12 5

indicators.note: accepting means the rest is held within the shortened country
not quite means the country loses its last letter

parts.note: Wales is a country of the UK
to alter is to change

indicators.note: restraining means the abbreviation for new is held inside the department

parts.note: MOD is the Ministry of Defence

explanation.surface: A nation resisting change, with a ministry holding back a new deputy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' trims the country to WALE, 'restraining' makes MOND, and 'accepting' holds the rest inside. 12 5 is VICE PRESIDENT: Walter Mondale served under Jimmy Carter.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter Mondale was Jimmy Carter's deputy, America's second in command from 1977 to 1981.

clue.text: Columnist, English chap after jewel in 12 5

indicators.note: after puts the abbreviation and the man behind the gem

parts.note: Nelson stands on top of Nelson's Column in London's Trafalgar Square
rock is slang for a gem or jewel
feller is an informal word for a chap

explanation.surface: A newspaper writer, an Englishman, chasing a gem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Columnist' looks like a journalist but is the admiral atop Nelson's Column in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelson Rockefeller was Gerald Ford's deputy, US second in command from 1974 to 1977.

clue.text: Pool, oxygen on top

indicators.note: on in an across clue means placed after, so the gas symbol follows the cover

parts.note: a lid is the top of a container
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A swimming pool with an oxygen supply above it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lido is a public open-air swimming pool, a British term for an outdoor pool.

clue.text: Third of mice forgets to retain squeak

indicators.note: third of picks out the third letter of the next word, mice

parts.note: to forget something is to lose it
to have something is to keep or retain it

explanation.surface: One mouse in three forgets how to keep its squeak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squeak' looks like a mouse's noise, but here it is a narrow escape.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow squeak is a near miss, so squeak alone means a narrow escape from danger.

clue.text: 12 5 gains power after catastrophe

indicators.note: after a catastrophe things are in ruins, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A deputy leader grows stronger after a disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 5 is VICE PRESIDENT, from the linked clue; the anagram of the two words of the surface's phrase is signalled by 'after catastrophe'.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiro Agnew was Richard Nixon's deputy, the US number two until he resigned in 1973.

clue.text: Question a command from cavalryman, perhaps

parts.note: who is a question word

explanation.surface: Querying an order given by a mounted soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Riders shout this to make a horse stop, so a cavalryman might give it as an order.

clue.text: Western food the pigs eat, not eastern rubbish

indicators.note: rubbish as a verb means to trash or mess up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Food that pigs eat, minus anything eastern, is garbage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' tells you to take E (eastern) out of THE PIGS EAT; 'rubbish' shuffles what is left. A cowboy film made in Italy is called a 'Western' of this pasta's name.
explanation.definitionFit: This pasta is a food, and Italian-made cowboy films are known as Westerns named after it.

clue.text: Some lothario tasting tiny bits

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A womaniser sampling small morsels.
explanation.definitionFit: Iota is the smallest Greek letter, so the word means a very small amount or jot.

clue.text: See 19
Russian conclusion? Job unfinished, as went beyond deadline

parts.note: -ov is a typical ending of Russian surnames, such as Romanov

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter of the word for a job is cut off

parts.note: an errand is a small job or task

explanation.surface: The Russian ending was a job left undone, as it overshot the deadline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Russian conclusion' is OV, a common ending of Russian surnames; ERRAND drops its D.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrun is to go past an allotted time, so the past tense means exceeded a deadline.
